title: Best one-piece swimsuits 2026: pool and beach
description: The $30 Cupshe and the $240 Norma Kamali trade places depending on what you care about.
lede: A swimsuit that looks great in the dressing room and sags at the back of the shoulder after three pool sessions is not a swimsuit — it is a disappointment with good marketing. This guide compares 5 options using published specifications, manufacturer documentation and independent reviews

sections.heading: How we compared
paragraphs: Colour retention is the most common long-term complaint in this category, and it splits the group clearly: the Cupshe draws the most fading reports after a season of pool and beach use, the Athleta the fewest.

Coverage confidence is judged from what owners describe across the everyday movements — sitting, bending, and wading into water. A suit that reviewers say needs constant readjustment, or that rides up in any of those movements, scored lower. This is the category where the Norma Kamali Mio earned its cult status.

sections.heading: Quick comparison
paragraphs: The table below covers the four most practical metrics for a swimsuit purchase. Prices are US MSRP in May 2026.

| Swimsuit | Price | Shape retention | Chlorine color retention | Size range |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cupshe | $35 | Weak — straps loosen fast | Low | S–3XL |
| Summersalt Sidestroke | $95 | Strong | Good | 16 cup sizes |
| Athleta One-Piece | $105 | Strong | Excellent | XS–3X |
| Norma Kamali Mio | $240 | Strong (hand wash only) | Good | XS–3XL |
| Andie The Malibu | $95 | Strong | Good | XS–2XL |

Strap tension is the thing most swimsuit reviews ignore. Once the straps relax, the back of the suit falls away from the shoulder blades — a fit problem that gets worse with every wash, and the single most common reason owners retire a suit early. If you swim more than twice a month, any suit that attracts repeated loose-strap complaints should be treated as a one-season purchase rather than a multi-year one.

sections.heading: Cupshe — best for fashion trend-chasers
paragraphs: Cupshe releases 100+ new styles each season at $30-45. If you want the swimsuit silhouette that is trending right now — ruched front, square neck, high cut leg — Cupshe will have it. At $35 it is the obvious choice for trend shoppers who rotate styles every 1-2 summers.

The performance trade-off is real. Straps that go slack after a handful of pool sessions are the most common Cupshe complaint in owner reviews, and lightening of the inner thigh panel in chlorinated water is the second. The suit still looks fine for casual beach use; it is not suited for regular pool training or if you expect it to hold its shape for more than one season.
Size range from S to 3XL is one of the widest here. The 100+ styles per season means you will find more variety in cut and coverage than any other brand in this comparison.

sections.heading: Summersalt Sidestroke — the functional fashion middle ground
paragraphs: Summersalt designed the Sidestroke around 16 cup sizes, which is the strongest size approach in this comparison. The built-in tummy control panel is present but not aggressive — it smooths rather than compresses. UPF 50+ coverage means this is also a valid beach session suit for extended sun exposure.

The recycled fabric construction holds up well in owner reports: straps that keep their tension through a season and no visible color change in chlorine. At $95 it sits in the middle of this comparison on price and at the top on size fit diversity.

The weakness is the color range — 12 colorways at the time of writing, versus Cupshe's 100+ styles. If finding a specific aesthetic is important to you, the Summersalt offers a curated selection rather than a broad one.

sections.heading: Athleta One-Piece — best for active swimming
paragraphs: Athleta built the Cali One-Piece for water movement, and the chlorine-resistant fabric is the part owners single out: fading complaints are rarer for this suit than for any other in the comparison, even from people swimming laps several times a week. Adjustable straps, full rear coverage, and construction designed to stay in place during actual laps.

At $105 it is the most expensive suit here after the Norma Kamali. The trade-off for the performance construction is a more athletic, less fashion-forward aesthetic. If your primary use is lap swimming or water sports, this is the correct pick. If you are primarily poolside or beach, the Andie or Norma Kamali are more flattering in a static setting.
12 color options are more restrained than Cupshe but cover the practical range. Adjustable back straps are a practical feature that none of the other suits in this comparison offer.

sections.heading: Norma Kamali Mio and Andie The Malibu
paragraphs: The Norma Kamali Mio has been in production since 1975 and the silhouette has not changed because it does not need to. Plunging neckline, ruched torso, and the coverage owners rate highest in this comparison across sit, bend, and wade movements. At $240 it is the most expensive suit here by $135.

The weakness is practical: at $240, a swimsuit that requires hand washing to keep its shape is an investment that demands care. Every other suit here is machine washable on gentle. The Norma Kamali requires cold hand wash and lay-flat dry — if you will not do that, the Andie at $95 delivers 80% of the aesthetic with standard care instructions.

Andie's The Malibu is the direct-to-consumer play in this comparison: 100% recycled fabric, sculpting liner, 10+ colors, and $95 price that is possible because there is no retail markup. The sculpting liner is more aggressive than the Summersalt's — full compression rather than smoothing.

faqs.q: How long should a one-piece swimsuit last before it needs replacing?
faqs.a: With regular care, a quality suit (Summersalt, Athleta, Andie) lasts 2-3 seasons of regular wear — 30-50 pool sessions. A fast-fashion suit like Cupshe typically attracts stretch and color-loss complaints inside a single season. The Norma Kamali, hand-washed and cared for, can last 5+ years.

faqs.q: Does built-in tummy control actually work in a swimsuit?
faqs.a: It smooths and redistributes rather than sculpts. The Summersalt Sidestroke has a light tummy control panel that reduces rolling and improves the silhouette without compression discomfort. The Andie Malibu's sculpting liner is more aggressive — full compression from waist to hip. Both are noticeable; neither changes body shape fundamentally.

faqs.q: What does chlorine actually do to swimsuit fabric over time?
faqs.a: Chlorine breaks down the elastane (spandex) component of swimsuit fabric, which is responsible for stretch recovery and shape retention. Suits with higher elastane percentages degrade faster in chlorine. The Athleta and Summersalt use chlorine-resistant fabric constructions that preserve elastane integrity longer — visible as better color retention and less strap stretch.

faqs.q: Which swimsuit works best for cup-size fitting?
faqs.a: Summersalt Sidestroke, which offers 16 dedicated cup sizes rather than generic S/M/L sizing. This is the most specific fit architecture in this comparison and the best option for anyone who has historically found swimsuit bust fit inconsistent.

faqs.q: Is a $240 swimsuit actually worth it over a $95 one?
faqs.a: For the Norma Kamali specifically, the value is in the silhouette and coverage confidence — it is the best-rated suit in this comparison on sit/bend/wade coverage and has been a design constant since 1975. At $240 it requires hand washing and deliberate care. If you will do that, it can last 5+ years. If you will machine wash it, buy the Andie at $95 instead.

faqs.q: Can I machine wash all of these swimsuits?
faqs.a: Four out of five: yes. The Cupshe, Summersalt, Athleta, and Andie are all machine washable on gentle cold. The Norma Kamali Mio requires cold hand wash and lay-flat drying to maintain the ruching and fabric integrity. Using a mesh laundry bag for machine-washable suits extends their life.

faqs.q: Which suit is best if I am swimming laps rather than lounging?
faqs.a: Athleta Cali One-Piece. It draws the fewest chlorine-fading complaints of the five, has adjustable straps for a secure fit during movement, and full rear coverage so nothing shifts during flip turns. The Summersalt Sidestroke is a good second choice for moderate lap swimming.

The trade-off is performance: slack straps and visible chlorine fading are the two complaints that dominate owner reviews inside a single season. This is a 1-2 season suit for trend shoppers, not a multi-year investment.

Great for occasional beach or vacation use
cons: Straps go slack quickly — the weakest shape retention here

The listed specs are UPF 50+ coverage and recycled fabric construction, and owners report the straps keep their tension and the color holds through a season of pool use. The color range is curated rather than broad.

Recycled fabric; owners report straps keep their tension

If you cannot commit to hand-washing the Norma Kamali, this is the aesthetic compromise that makes sense.
